# git: command: push the branch and tags atomically

**Motivation:** `git push` (`git-push` in `bin/lib/git/sync.bash`) sends the branch and all tags in one command, but not atomically: the server accepts or rejects each ref on its own. When the branch is rejected (non-fast-forward, branch protection) and a new release tag is accepted, the tag lands on a commit that is not on the branch, and a tag-triggered release runs from it or fails, leaving a published tag to clean up by hand. `git force` (`bin/git_force`) has the same shape with `-f`.

**Proposal:** push the branch and the tags as one transaction:

```bash
git push --atomic --tags "${remote}" "${branch}"
```

Either every ref is updated or none is.

**Trade-off:** `--tags` sends every local tag, so a single stale or conflicting local tag now blocks the branch too, where today the branch goes through and only that tag fails. Release guardrails that inspect pushed tags (e.g. a `pre-push` hook refusing a release tag without a changelog note) see all of them as well.

**Related issues:**

- [[DOT-355]] — `git force` / `git please` refactoring, same push policy question.
- octomation/makefiles#81 — versioned `pre-push` hooks that rely on the branch and the tag arriving in one push.

<!-- 2026-09-23T13:53Z https://github.com/kamilsk/dotfiles/issues/884#issuecomment-5796102183
Alternative: send only the tags that belong to the pushed commits.

```bash
git push --atomic --follow-tags "${remote}" "${branch}"
```

Pros:

- only annotated tags reachable from the pushed commits go out; stray, stale or experimental local tags stay local and can no longer block the branch;
- a `pre-push` release guardrail sees just the tags of this push;
- the same command fits `git release` (#885), so both share one push policy.

Cons:

- lightweight tags are never pushed; with `tag.gpgSign` on, `git tag vX` is signed and therefore annotated, but a tag created with `--no-sign` or by a tool stays behind silently;
- a tag on a commit that is not in the pushed branch (e.g. on another branch) is not sent; today `--tags` sends it;
- tags deleted or moved on purpose are not propagated either way; that remains `git untag` / `git force` territory.

`push.followTags true` in `bin/git_config` would make the same behaviour the default for plain `git push`, at the cost of the same caveats everywhere.
-->

<!-- 2026-09-23T14:19Z https://github.com/kamilsk/dotfiles/issues/884#issuecomment-5796527355
Correction to the comment above: `--follow-tags` does not keep stray tags local when they are annotated. It sends every annotated tag that points at a pushed commit and is missing on the remote, and with `tag.gpgSign` on every tag made by `git tag` is signed, hence annotated. So it narrows the set (only tags on pushed commits), but an experimental signed tag on the branch still goes out. Only an explicit refspec sends exactly one tag, which is what #885 does for releases.

Relation: independent of #885 — `git release` does not rely on this policy; this issue is about plain `git push` / `git force` (see #356).
